About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• 
Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• 
Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• 
Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• 
Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• 
Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• 
Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• 
Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• 
Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• 
A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• 
Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• 
Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• 
Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• 
Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• 
Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• 
Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• 
Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• 
Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like for the Team You'll Join

• 
Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• 
Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• 
Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• 
The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

• 
The opportunity to shape the voice of a high-impact climate technology company in one of its first markets.

• 
A central role in connecting Photoncycle's customers, product and brand.

• 
A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant ownership.

• 
An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BLOXhub with lunch benefits and unlimited coffee.

Photoncycle is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience, and potential.

About AutoUncle

Buying a used car is one of the biggest purchases most people make, and one of the hardest to get right. Is the price fair? What will it really cost? AutoUncle was founded to answer those questions. Today, car buyers across Europe use our websites and apps to compare almost every used car for sale and see whether the price is right, for free.

The car dealerships that sell to those buyers are our customers. Over 700 of them use AutoUncle to sell more cars. We send them buyers who are ready to act, and we put tools on their websites that turn visitors into leads.

Now we're going a step further. CoDriver, our newest product, is an AI assistant that answers every lead a dealer gets, on every channel, day or night, and keeps the conversation going until the buyer is ready. We're no longer just sending buyers to dealers; we're helping them close the sale.

Why we’re hiring

AutoUncle is growing fast. More dealers are signing up, and more of them are choosing CoDriver, which connects directly to their CRM, lead providers and website. Every new customer means a new setup to get right and keep running.

The Digital Operations Team

That's where our Digital Operations Team comes in. Sales wins the customer; Digital Operations makes our products work for them. The team gets new dealers live, keeps their integrations healthy and fixes issues quickly when something breaks. A dealer only sees value once leads are flowing, so this team has a direct hand in whether customers stay and grow with us.

The team works across Denmark, Germany and Italy, and we're looking to add someone in the near future to our DACH team to support our growth in the region.

Your mission

Own the technical setup for a portfolio of 60–80 DACH customers, from first call to go-live and beyond. Make sure every product we deliver is properly integrated, measurable from day one, and keeps working.

Day to day, you’ll:

• 
Lead technical onboardings. Connect our products with dealer websites, CRM systems and inventory feeds, and coordinate more complex or tailored integrations.

• 
Join customer meetings alongside Sales, answer technical questions in German and set clear expectations on feasibility and go-live timelines.

• 
Pick up the phone to unblock setups. Reach out to web agencies, CRM providers and dealer IT contacts to solve problems quickly.

• 
Diagnose tracking and data issues. Investigate GA4, Google Tag Manager, consent mode and event tracking when numbers don’t add up, and find out why, not just what.

• 
Customize and improve. Adjust widgets with custom CSS and improve our standard integrations to give customers’ website visitors a better experience.

• 
Keep your portfolio healthy with regular health checks, inventory quality checks and proactive monitoring.

• 
Build repeatable systems. Turn recurring problems into standard workflows, documentation, and AI workflows and automations the whole team uses, and work with product and tech colleagues to drive improvements.

What you bring

• 
Native or near-native German, and fluent English (our company language)

• 
2+ years of experience in technical integrations, implementation, digital operations or a similar role, ideally in B2B SaaS

• 
Hands-on experience with web analytics and tracking (GA4, Google Tag Manager or similar). You understand events, conversions and consent mode well enough to troubleshoot them

• 
A basic understanding of APIs and how systems exchange data

• 
HTML/CSS skills for adjusting and troubleshooting website integrations

• 
Confidence picking up the phone and working with both technical (developers, CRM providers) and non-technical (dealers, sales teams) contacts

• 
A structured way of working: you run several setups at once, prioritize your own pipeline and follow through without being chased

• 
You already use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT or similar) to get real work done, and you can tell us about something you automated or made faster.

Nice to have:

• 
Experience in the automotive industry or at a web agency

• 
Experience with HubSpot or dealer CRM systems

What we offer

• 
€54,600–67,800 gross annual (final salary depending on experience)

• 
Extended social benefits; including 30 holiday days + local holidays, extended parental leave, etc. See more in our Employee Handbook!

• 
Structured training in your first three months, alongside experienced teammates, on our products (Traffic Performance, Website Booster and CoDriver),and how dealerships work

• 
A clear path to Senior Digital Operations Manager, by owning a specialist area such as data quality, website tracking or partner integrations

• 
A growth review every six months and support from your manager to plan your next step

• 
Impact you can see: when a dealer goes live and the leads start coming in, you made that happen

How we work

We're AI-native, and you'll help shape how we use AI in customer operations.

AutoUncle moves fast, and priorities can change from week to week. If you haven't worked somewhere like this before, that's fine. If the idea sounds exciting rather than stressful, you'll fit right in.

We hire for four traits we call "the Ticket": being ambitious, humble and coachable, with a bias for action. We also live by the Five Cs: Clear, Courage, Curiosity, Commitment and Compassion. Our Employee Handbook gives a good feel for how we work.

The process

• 
Intro call with our Talent Acquisition team

• 
Interview with the hiring managers, conducted in English. Then a short conversation in German with a team member

• 
A short personality test (online, in your own time), followed by a case interview where you’ll also meet the team

• 
Reference checks

Our predictive models estimate the condition and remaining lifespan of building components, and we turn that into prioritised maintenance plans across entire portfolios. Our AI agent, Tily, can take action on users' behalf and help them run strategic analysis of their building portfolio, helping large property owners and managers maintain their buildings efficiently, cost-effectively and sustainably.

The product went live in 2024 and is already solving real problems for real people, with customers across Denmark, Norway, and Germany. There is still so much we can do to make it even better, and you could help shape the future of building maintenance – and how engineering is run at proprty.ai.

What we're looking for

We're looking for a player-coach who loves leading engineers and still wants to write code. You might coach a developer through a tricky problem in the morning and ship a feature yourself in the afternoon.

You've led an engineering team before at a startup or scale-up where the foundations were still being laid, and you know that in a small team, leadership means leading by doing. You care about shipping fast and shipping well.

We're an AI-first company (it's in our name). You've built AI agents and AI features into real products, and you're excited to push that further, both in what we build for customers and in how the team works.

We're a small but mighty crew of four engineers who love solving tricky problems together, working on-site in our office near Rådhuspladsen. We work closely with our data science team to bring machine learning models trained on millions of m² of building data into the product. Help turn input from customers, Sales and Customer Success into features the team can build

Improve the team's AI tools and workflows (we use Cursor and Perplexity) so everyone can build faste

About you

You've led an engineering team before at a startup or scale-up, including coaching and hiring developers

You have strong hands-on full-stack experience with React, TypeScript and SQL

• 
You've built (or have strong interest in) AI agents and AI features in production

• 
You take full ownership from design to implementation, and you lead by doing

• 
You live in the Copenhagen area (we're in the office 4 days a week)

• 
Bonus points if you've worked with Postgres and Next.js, or in real estate or proptech

Even if you don't tick every box, we'd still love to hear from you if you're an experienced engineering leader who learns fast and loves building things!

Would you like to become the technical go-to person for the systems that keep a fleet of working vessels accurate and operational? At HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor, you will take ownership of dredging systems, survey equipment and onboard IT across the fleet, with plenty of freedom to shape how the area is run.

Take technical ownership across the fleet

HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor has delivered marine construction projects since 1958 and today works across Northern Europe within dredging, offshore wind, coastal protection and maritime infrastructure.

As the fleet grows, HØJ wants to bring more technical knowledge in-house. You will join the technical team in Horsens, where you will take specialist responsibility for the systems connecting dredging operations, positioning, survey equipment and onboard IT. While your colleagues cover other technical areas across the fleet, your primary focus will be the dredging systems and the related IT and survey technology.

Your main focus will be the 3D dredging systems across seven vessels, including Teledyne PDS, positioning equipment, sensors and the supporting IT setup. You will work closely with skippers, crews, project managers and suppliers and become the person they turn to when systems need to be set up, improved or brought back online.

Some days, you will work alongside your colleagues in the technical team in Horsens, planning and coordinating maintenance, configuring systems or supporting vessels remotely. Other days, you will be on board troubleshooting equipment, preparing a vessel for a new project or carrying out planned service and maintenance.

The aim is not only to solve problems when they occur, but to create a more consistent, well-documented and reliable setup across the fleet.

More specifically, you will:

• Take technical ownership of the fleet’s dredging systems and Teledyne PDS setup

• Work with positioning, sensors, multibeam and other survey equipment

• Support and improve onboard IT, networks and communication systems

• Plan preventive maintenance, calibrations and service

• Document the technical setup on each vessel and prepare relevant reports

• Support crews and project managers with troubleshooting and project preparation

One of your first tasks will be to map the existing system landscape across the vessels. You will also help commission the dredging system on a new vessel and establish clearer standards across the fleet.

Leading the commissioning strategy, team and schedule from mobilisation to integrated systems testing.

**Role Overview

**The Commissioning Manager leads Sensori's commissioning function on a project, ensuring mechanical and electrical systems are started, tested and proven safely, in the right sequence and to the client's acceptance criteria. The role develops the commissioning plan and schedule, manages commissioning engineers and vendor resources, controls the interface with the client's commissioning agent, and integrates commissioning requirements into the construction program so that handover is predictable and fully documented.

**Principal Duties And Responsibilities

**

• Develop and own the project commissioning plan, including strategy, organisation, level definitions, sequences, acceptance criteria and documentation requirements.

• Build and maintain the commissioning schedule; integrate it with the construction program and drive readiness of systems and areas to support it.

• Lead, allocate and develop the team of commissioning engineers; coordinate vendor and subcontractor commissioning resources.

• Chair commissioning coordination meetings with construction, quality, Authorised Persons, vendors and the client's commissioning agent.

• Oversee development and approval of method statements, checklists, test scripts and integrated systems test procedures.

• Manage the energisation and start-up sequence in conjunction with the Senior Authorised Person, ensuring permits, isolations and safety controls are in place.

• Monitor test execution, witness critical tests and ensure results are recorded, reviewed and accepted in the commissioning management system.

• Manage the commissioning issues log; drive closure of deficiencies with construction teams, subcontractors and vendors.

• Plan and lead integrated systems testing, including failure scenarios and redundancy demonstrations, with the client and third parties.

• Ensure complete, accurate turnover packages, training and documentation are delivered for handover.

• Report commissioning progress, risks and constraints to project leadership weekly; contribute to lessons learned and improvement of Sensori's commissioning standards.

• Support pre-construction and tenders with commissioning strategies, durations and resource plans.

**Selection criteria / person specification

**

• Degree in Mechanical, Electrical or Building Services Engineering, or a trade qualification with extensive commissioning leadership experience.

• At least seven years in commissioning, including several years leading commissioning teams on data centre, pharmaceutical or mission-critical projects.

• Strong understanding of both mechanical and electrical systems, sequences of operation and integrated testing.

• Experience working with client commissioning agents and formal level-based commissioning processes.

• Proven ability to plan and schedule commissioning within a construction program and to manage readiness across trades.

• Familiarity with commissioning management software and structured documentation.

• Strong leadership, coordination and communication skills; able to chair meetings and influence senior stakeholders.

• Sound knowledge of safe systems of work for energisation and live testing.

• Willing to travel and to be site-based for extended periods.

Mechanical Engineer – FLOWVISION A/S

About FLOWVISION A/S

FLOWVISION A/S is a Danish engineering company founded in 2006, specialized in designing and delivering advanced emission abatement systems for combustion-based power plants worldwide. Since 2021, the company has been part of AXENS GROUP, while continuing to operate as an independent business with its own organization, commercial responsibility, and market-facing role.

The company operates in an international EPC environment and delivers technically advanced solutions to customers within the energy, oil & gas, and industrial sectors across multiple global markets. FLOWVISION collaborates closely with major international players and is recognized for its strong technical know-how, high-quality standards, and ability to solve complex engineering challenges.

Today, FLOWVISION employs around 20 highly skilled specialists, creating a strong concentration of technical competencies and deep industry expertise. This gives the company the agility and close collaboration of a small expert team, combined with the backing and broader industrial context of being part of Axens.

FLOWVISION offers a flat organizational structure, short decision-making processes, and a collaborative culture where openness, knowledge sharing, and teamwork are essential parts of everyday life.

The company is currently experiencing significant growth and a strong order intake, creating attractive opportunities for professionals who want to influence both project execution and the continued development of the business.

The position

As Mechanical Engineer, you will become part of FLOWVISION’s highly specialized engineering environment and play a key role in the execution of technically advanced international EPC projects.

You will work closely with our Lead Mechanical Engineer, Project Managers, workshops, suppliers, and external engineering partners to ensure that mechanical designs, fabrication documentation, and technical solutions are delivered with high quality and according to demanding project timelines.

The role combines hands-on engineering with close interaction across fabrication, welding, procurement, and project execution activities. You will contribute throughout the entire project lifecycle — from bid clarification and design reviews to fabrication support, inspections, and final documentation.

This is a role for someone who enjoys solving practical engineering challenges, working close to production realities, and operating in an environment where technical quality, collaboration, and execution are critical to success.

You will also have the opportunity to influence engineering processes and contribute to the continued professionalization and growth of the business.

Key responsibilities

Mechanical project execution

• Participate in technical reviews of RFQ packages and specifications during bidding and project execution phases.

• Support clarification processes and ensure alignment of technical scope, assumptions, and interfaces.

• Define mechanical design requirements and coordinate engineering inputs towards external engineering and drafting partners.

• Work with mechanical drawings and technical documentation, including general arrangements, structural steel drawings, piping layouts, isometrics, and fabrication documentation.

• Support structured engineering milestone reviews and contribute to design acceptance and design freeze activities.

• Identify and resolve technical issues, deviations, and design changes throughout the project lifecycle.

• Assess manufacturability and propose practical engineering improvements related to fabrication, welding, installation, and assembly.

Fabrication, welding & workshop interface

• Act as a daily technical interface towards workshops and fabrication partners.

• Handle technical clarifications during fabrication and pre-assembly activities.

• Participate in workshop activities such as PIM, pre-FAT, FAT, inspections, and technical follow-up.

• Support resolution of punch items, deviations, and non-conformities together with Project Management and QHSE.

Documentation & engineering coordination

• Prepare and consolidate mechanical engineering documentation for customer deliveries.

• Work actively with engineering data, revisions, BOM structures, and document control processes.

• Support procurement activities through technical review of supplier quotations and deviations.

• Contribute to maintaining technical quality, traceability, and compliance across all project phases.

Qualifications

We expect you to have:

• A technical degree within Mechanical Engineering or a similar engineering discipline.

• Experience from project-based engineering environments, fabrication, workshops, or EPC project execution.

• Practical exposure to welding, piping, valves, structural steel, or process equipment.

• Strong ability to read, review, and assess mechanical and fabrication drawings.

• Familiarity with relevant standards such as ASME and EN1090.

• Experience working with AutoCAD or similar 2D/3D CAD systems. Plant3D is preferred.

• Experience working with drawings, revisions, BOM structures, and document management systems.

• A structured, analytical, and proactive mindset with strong attention to detail.

• The ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, quality, procurement, and project functions.

• Strong English communication skills, written and spoken. Danish is considered an advantage.

Practical information

• Location: FLOWVISION A/S, Odense, Denmark

• Reporting line: COO / Lead Mechanical Engineer

• Travel activity: Approx. 20–30 days annually depending on projects

What we offer

FLOWVISION offers a unique opportunity to become part of a highly specialized and growing international engineering company where technical know-how and collaboration are the core drivers of success.

We offer:

• A key technical role in an international and rapidly growing engineering company.

• The opportunity to work on technically advanced and highly challenging international EPC projects.

• A unique environment with a strong concentration of specialist competencies and technical expertise.

• Excellent opportunities for professional and personal development as the company continues its growth and professionalization journey.

• A high degree of influence on engineering solutions, project execution, and ways of working.

• A flat organization with fast decision-making and close collaboration across the company.

• A versatile and dynamic workday characterized by openness, cooperation, flexibility, and humor.

• A strong development culture with high ambitions regarding quality, innovation, and employee well-being.

FLOWVISION is a company where highly skilled people work closely together to deliver complex solutions to global customers — and where the right person will have the opportunity to make a visible impact on both projects and the future development of the business.

At Acodyne, you will help develop the software, high-power electronics, and robotic systems that bring our next generation of high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAS to life, moving between code, schematics, the lab bench, and real flight hardware.

Your Role

You will work closely with our CTO and engineering team on the electrical and software systems that power and control our aircraft. From firmware to high-power distribution, this is as real as engineering gets. You will:

• 
Develop and test embedded software and firmware for flight-critical and ground systems (C/C++, Python)

• 
Design, build, and test high-power electronics such as power distribution, battery systems, and motor drives

• 
Integrate sensors, actuators, and robotic/autonomous subsystems into the aircraft and ground equipment

• 
Develop tools for test automation, data logging, and analysis

• 
Bring up, debug, and validate hardware on the bench and during flight tests

• 
Document designs, code, and test results for certification purposes

About You

You enjoy writing code as much as holding an oscilloscope probe or a soldering iron. You're the type who builds things outside class and wants to take that to the next level. You likely:

• 
Are currently pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, software/computer engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or similar

• 
Have programming experience in C/C++ and/or Python

• 
Have a solid understanding of electronics and circuit design

• 
Enjoy hands-on lab work, prototyping, and debugging real hardware

• 
Are curious about UAVs, robotics, or high-performance systems

• 
Are proactive, independent, and eager to learn fast

Nice to have:

Experience with power electronics, high-voltage systems, motor control, or battery management systems (BMS)

• 
Experience with embedded platforms (STM32, ARM, etc.), RTOS, or communication buses (CAN, UART, SPI, I²C)

• 
Exposure to ROS, PX4/ArduPilot, or control and autonomy algorithms

• 
PCB design experience (KiCad, Altium, etc.)

About Acodyne

We are a UAS company developing heavy-lift, high-speed eVTOL UAS for defence and industrial logistics. We are currently 18 people, based at our workshop at Avedøre Airfield, and plan to double our team in the next year.

About the Internship

• 
Duration: Full-time for 5–6 months, with start in January/February 2027.

• 
Time off: 2.08 vacation days per month + Danish public holidays.

• 
Location: Avedøre Flyveplads, workshop-based, approximately 45 minutes by public transport from Copenhagen city center.

• 
Compensation: DKK 6,000-8,000 per month before tax. Please note this is a contribution to living and transport. It will likely not cover full living costs. Interns are expected to supplement with grants or other funding.

Please note: The internship opportunity is intended for currently enrolled students who wish to gain relevant work experience as part of their studies. We particularly encourage applications from students who are able to use the internship as an integrated part of their degree programme, for example through ECTS credits, a project-based internship, or another formal study-related arrangement.

jobs.occupation: Data Platform Engineer – Offshore Wind Industry
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about building and running reliable, scalable and secure cloud data platforms? Do you want to work in the offshore wind industry, where your engineering skills will help secure a sustainable future based on renewable energy? Then keep reading: Cadeler is looking for a Data Platform Engineer with your skills and interests!

Cadeler is a global partner in the offshore wind industry, specializing in wind farm construction and maintenance. Our industry is more relevant than ever and plays a critical role in the energy transition, with a strong long-term outlook. As our industry continues to develop, so do we!

We are now looking for a Data Platform Engineer to help build, automate and operate our cloud data platform, ensuring that trusted and well-governed data is available for analytics, reporting and operational decision-making.

**What will you do?

**As our Data Platform Engineer, you will design, build and operate the technical foundations of Cadeler's data platform on Snowflake and Azure. You will work with business teams, application owners, IT and information security to integrate source systems, automate data pipelines and make reliable data available for analytics and reporting.

**Your Main Tasks Include

**

• Design, build and maintain data pipelines from various source systems, using managed ingestion tools such as Fivetran and custom Python where connectors fall short

• Orchestrate and schedule pipelines, handle dependencies, retries and backfills, and manage Snowflake warehouse sizing and compute cost

• Own CI/CD and source control in Azure DevOps: branching strategy, PR reviews, automated deployments and environment promotion (dev, test, prod), with database objects and infrastructure managed as code

• Design and implement dimensional data models (facts, dimensions, star schemas, slowly changing dimensions) across raw, staging, integration and mart layers

• Set up pipeline monitoring, anomaly detection and alerting, and troubleshoot and resolve incidents in production

• Deliver curated, performant datasets and semantic-ready measures so departments can build reports in Power BI

**To Succeed In This Role

**Being part of the Cadeler community means having a natural interest in and care for the environment, and in our shared mission to speed up the green energy transition. Environmental considerations and the safety of our people and the planet will be a key priority in your daily work.

We are looking for an innovator with a solution-oriented mind, who thrives in a fast-paced environment with many different interfaces.

We think you will be a good match if you have:

• A university degree in a relevant area such as computing, statistics or mathematics

• 3+ years of hands-on experience as a data engineer or data platform engineer

• Proven experience designing, building and operating production data pipelines

• Advanced SQL skills and strong Python skills for data processing, automation and tooling, and experience with dimensional modelling

• Hands-on experience with Snowflake (warehouses, RBAC, storage and compute management, cost control) and the Azure ecosystem

• An understanding of data security, governance and access control principles, as well as ability to define and write logic that transforms raw data into useful, interpretable, business-driven datasets

• Fluent spoken and written English

**Come work with us!

**By becoming a Cadeler employee, you will be part of a rapidly growing company with a diverse and energetic team. We offer an exciting position focused on delivering excellence in the face of interesting new challenges, within a positive and rewarding work environment in an international company with great development possibilities.

Cadeler is headquartered in Copenhagen, with offices in Vejle, Norwich, Rotterdam and Taipei, as well as colleagues working offshore aboard our fleet of Wind Farm Installation Vessels (WFIV).

Meet some of our colleagues here: https://www.cadeler.com/career

**Apply

**Use the APPLY button to apply for this position. For data protection purposes, applications are only accepted via the link and are assessed continuously until we find the right candidate, so please don't hesitate to send in your application as soon as possible and no later than the 6th of November.

If you have any questions about the position, and/or for practical matters, please contact peopleandculture@cadeler.com.

Then you might be the Technical Project Manager we are looking for in our Customer Services team at Körber Supply Chain.

As our new Technical Project Manager, you will be responsible for managing and delivering minor and middle size Customer service project with a variety in complexity from initial order intake through execution and successful Delivery. Furthermore, you will oversee the procurement of equipment, components, and resources, monitor project finances, manage changes in project scope and priorities, and ensure that all deliverables meet customer expectations and agreed performance targets.

The position requires a structured and analytical professional who can balance technical detail with commercial understanding. You are comfortable working independently, taking ownership of your projects, and navigating complex situations while maintaining focus on deadlines, quality, and customer satisfaction. You enjoy building relationships and collaborating across functions and cultures, and you are able to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

We imagine that you have 3-5 years of experience from a similar project management role, preferably within a technical, industrial, automation, or engineering environment. You possess a strong technical understanding and are comfortable reviewing and working with technical documentation and system specifications. Experience with project management tools is expected, and fluency in Danish and English is required. As some projects involve on-site activities, a willingness to travel is also important.

At Körber Supply Chain, you will become part of an international organization and a highly skilled Customer Services team where collaboration, professionalism, and continuous improvement are key. This position is also an important part of the planned succession within our Customer Services Sales & Specialist team. Through close collaboration with experienced colleagues, you will gain valuable knowledge and insight, ensuring a strong foundation for future success in the role.

We offer an exciting role in an international company in growth, where you will work with advanced technical solutions and be part of a strong professional environment characterized by collaboration and dedication. We offer a range of attractive employee benefits:

Social Events: We have a strong company culture that we invest heavily in maintaining and developing. This includes a wide range of events and an active employee association that organizes activities such as Friday bars, Christmas parties, an annual ski trip, cultural events, and much more!

Körber is a global technology company for intelligent manufacturing and supply chain solutions. As a reliable innovation partner, Körber turns entrepreneurial thinking into customer success by providing leading technology to fuel what’s next – from end-to-end pharma production and advanced supply chain solutions to high-tech machinery and process equipment. Körber combines deep domain expertise with integrated hardware, software, and digital services, to help customers take the next step.

The role

We are looking for a Product Manager to join our Product Management team in Aarhus.

The team is still being built. Today, problem framing, epic work, roadmap, customer dialogue and design coordination sit in one place. That limits how many product tracks we can run properly at the same time. You give us the capacity to go deep on several at once, so we can move from reacting to demand to driving a coherent product.

We serve four markets and four customer types with one platform. That takes discipline about what becomes configuration and what becomes a special build. Holding that line, with a rationale that also holds up in front of a customer, is a real part of the job.

We work AI-augmented. Modern AI tools take more of the writing and synthesis off your desk, which makes judgement the valuable work: which problem is real, what we build, and what we decline. We use AI to move faster, and we believe people are what make sure we build the right things.

Your work reaches hundreds of thousands of people across the Nordics: job seekers navigating labour market reforms, employment professionals adapting to new digitalisation strategies, and the institutions managing that change.

What you will work on

Candeno serves municipalities, unemployment funds, and educational institutions across Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland. The platform has three sides: candidates navigating the labour market, advisors guiding them through digitalisation and compliance workflows, and companies recruiting talent. One platform, many contexts.

To begin with, the role is deliberately broad. You work across customers, markets, segments and products, wherever the need is greatest. A fixed ownership area is set as the team grows. You will:

Discovery and problem framing

• 
Turn input from customers, Customer Success, sales and Product Support into qualified problem statements.

• 
Run and facilitate user interviews, workshops and validation together with design.

• 
Understand the problem before the solution, and get discovery done before we estimate.

Definition and delivery

• 
Write epics and solution descriptions others can build on, with scope, boundaries and success criteria.

• 
Prioritise and drive the backlog together with engineering and architecture.

• 
Follow deliveries all the way out: release notes, internal enablement, and follow-up on real impact.

Customer and market dialogue

• 
Take part in customer dialogue and workshops with Customer Success and sales, without committing to functionality on the spot.

• 
Assess feature requests across customers: what is one customer's edge case, and what is a shared need.

Direction and communication

• 
Contribute to roadmap, themes and horizons (Now, Next, Later).

• 
Make sure cross-cutting dependencies such as integrations, data and compliance are understood before we commit to building.

Your mandate

You prioritise within an agreed direction, you can say no to special builds, and you decide within your own track. Overall direction, cross-cutting prioritisation and roadmap commitments sit with the Head of Product Management.

Who we are looking for

You are a product manager who loves the problem. You go deep on the challenge before you reach for a solution, you write clearly enough that other people can act on it, and you are comfortable in an organisation where the frame is not finished yet.

You will need:

• 
Experience as a Product Manager or Product Owner on a SaaS product.

• 
The ability to run discovery independently: talk to users, synthesise what you hear, and turn it into problems and requirements.

• 
Clear and structured writing. Epics, problem statements and decision papers other people can act on.

• 
Experience working closely with engineers and designers in a team with real ownership.

• 
Danish and English at working level, written and spoken.

Nice to have:

• 
Knowledge of the employment sector, public sector customers, or other regulated domains.

• 
Experience with multi-tenant products, configurability and white-label.

• 
Experience with B2G sales and decision processes, where a decision takes 6 to 24 months and involves many stakeholders.

• 
A considered approach to AI in your own product work, including judgement about when the output needs verifying.

• 
Enough understanding of integrations and data models to ask the right questions.

The kind of person who does well here:

• 
Loves the problem. Goes deep on the challenge before the solution.

• 
Self-driven where the frame is not finished, and helps build it.

• 
Honest and direct, including when the answer is no, or not yet.

• 
Has empathy for all three parties: the job seeker, the advisor and the customer.

• 
Comfortable with breadth, and with switching between segments and markets.

• 
Collaborates rather than hands over.

What the first six months look like

After one month

You know the platform as a user, on both the candidate and the advisor side, and you can explain what we solve and for whom. You have met product, design, engineering, Customer Success and sales, and you know who to go to when. You have listened in on customer dialogue and support cases across all three customer segments, and you have taken ownership of a first, well-defined problem.

After three months

You run discovery independently on your own tracks and deliver problem statements and epics the team can build on. You have taken at least one delivery from problem to release and followed up on the impact. You contribute credibly to prioritisation, you can turn down a special build with a rationale that holds, and you handle customer dialogue independently alongside Customer Success.

After six months

You have full ownership of one or more product areas and you are the team's go-to person on them. You contribute to roadmap and direction, not only to execution. You have moved a measurable outcome for customers or users, and you have changed something about how we work, not only about the product.

Working at Candeno

We are a scale-up. That means real ownership, real impact, and a product that is still being shaped by the people who work on it.

We are based in Aarhus, and this is an on-site role. You report to the Head of Product Management and work in a product trio with design and architecture throughout, close to engineering, Customer Success, sales and Product Support.

Our product philosophy follows Cagan and SVPG: outcome-oriented teams, discovery before estimation, and configurability over special builds. We work in ClickUp for epics and backlog, Figma and FigJam for design and concept work, and Freshdesk for release communication. We work in Danish and English. Swedish and Norwegian are handled together with colleagues.

We are direct and focused on doing the right thing for users. We share work early and expect you to do the same.

What we offer

• 
Pension scheme and health insurance

• 
5 extra days off after 2 years of seniority (10 in total)

• 
Daily lunch from Meyers Madhus

• 
A shared milestone programme that celebrates successes big and small

• 
An active social life: team events, clubs, and an engaged social committee

The process

• 
A short screening call with the Head of Product Management

• 
A first interview with the Head of Product Management and the CTO, a deeper conversation about your experience and the role

• 
A case interview, a practical brief sent in advance

No cover letter. You will answer three short questions when you apply.

About Candeno

Candeno is a Nordic employment technology company based in Aarhus. We build the platform that connects candidates, advisors, and companies across municipalities, unemployment funds, and educational institutions in Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland. Our work sits at the intersection of public sector compliance and modern product thinking, and we take both seriously.
